_description: A generic two-handled controller, computed for this pack and held in the device frame (x to the right as the user sees the face, y toward the top edge, z out of the face toward the user, mm). The body is 150 x 60 x 22 mm (x -75..75, y -40..20, z -22..0), with a 36 mm handle under each end, gripped at (+/-60, -50, -18). Each thumb works a stick, a pad or a cluster of four buttons and a small key near the middle; each index finger works a bumper on the top edge; a power key in the middle of the top edge is pressed after a regrip. Mirror-symmetric about x = 0. The users are 18 and older. ergo.digit_reach counts 97.96% of the 2,208 women and 99.72% of the 1,774 men of ANSUR 1988 reaching every judged control (btn_y limits for the women), against the claim's >= 95%.

hand_controls.regrip_reason: pressed once per session, by either hand

_claims.statement: At least 95% of the women and 95% of the men in ANSUR 1988 can reach every control pressed from its grip without regripping

_notes.hand_grips: Where each hand holds the device, a list of {id, centre, hand_axis, handle_axis} in the device frame. centre: the point on the handle's axis where the middle finger wraps it, mm. hand_axis: the direction from the wrist to the hand with the wrist straight (any length; made unit). handle_axis: the handle's long axis (any length). The hand axis must lie within 20 deg of perpendicular to the handle axis: wrist-centre of grip length was measured with the handle square to the fist.
_notes.hand_controls: Every control a hand presses, a list of {id, at, operated_by, regrip_reason}. at: the centre of the pressed top surface, mm, device frame. operated_by: the grips and digits that press it without a regrip, [{grip, digit}] with digit thumb, index or other; a thumb or index control is judged, an other-only control (a paddle under the middle finger) is counted and not judged. A control pressed only after a regrip has operated_by [] and must say why in regrip_reason; it is listed, not judged.
_notes.hand_grip_diameter_mm: The largest handle's perimeter divided by pi, through its grip centre, mm. Operating context 25 to 50 mm (the cylinders Kong and Lowe 2005 tested): outside it a pass does not count. A larger value puts every wrist farther back, so a device with two different handles states the larger. No alias: the spine judges the context on the spelling the gate read.
_notes.hand_user_age_min_years: The youngest intended user, years. Operating context 17 and over (ANSUR 1988's subjects are 17 to 51): a pass for children does not count, and an absent value reads as outside the context. No alias.
_notes._claims: the claim the baseline was calibrated against. ergo.digit_reach reads its limit from the claim tagged digit-reach (ctx.acceptance), as a share of subjects in %. 95% is the usual human-factors target (design for all but the 5% of smallest hands); the baseline passes at 97.96% and the known-bad cluster, moved 10 mm up the face, fails at 63.09%.
_notes._aliases: none. The context keys take none by rule, and the two lists name their object; bare spellings such as controls or grips would collide with other packs' vocabularies.
